items.title: OpenRouter 重建默认路由算法：TTFT 降 16.9%、429 错误减少 67%
items.description: OpenRouter 宣布重建默认 provider 路由算法，从只按价格排序改为按 Routing Cost 综合 effective price、TTFT、吞吐、错误率和输出质量选路。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/l4znfnzfs6rz6vorl1wyj90gb
items.excerpt:
How we rebuilt provider routing for better, faster inference
OpenRouter 宣布重建默认 provider 路由算法，从只按价格排序改为按 Routing Cost 综合 effective price、TTFT、吞吐、错误率和输出质量选路。
OpenRouter 自己公布的路由算法实测数据与机制细节，读者可据此评估默认路由切换对现有调用成本和延迟的实际影响。
今天，我们宣布对提供商路由算法进行自 OpenRouter 成立以来最大的一次升级。
此前，我们的默认路由器主要只奖励提供商一件事：低价。新路由器奖励的是真正对你最有利的推理：便宜，同时还要快、吞吐量高、可靠。能提供更多价值的提供商会自动赢得更多流量，因此每个提供商都有动力持续改进。这意味着你通过 OpenRouter 获得的推理会越来越快、越来越可靠、越来越划算，而你一行代码都不用改。
它已经见效了。新算法带来了显著改善：TTFT 提升 16.9%，吞吐量提升 16.3%，容量错误大幅减少 67%！而成本仅小幅上升 6.0%。这还是在提供商尚未有时间针对新算法进行优化的情况下取得的。更多细节请查看完整的 实验结果 。
路由仍然会考虑缓存，因此一旦我们把你发送到某个提供商，只要缓存还是热的，你的会话就会留在那里。
想要仅按价格路由？仍然可以。请参阅 保持不变的部分 中关于固定和排序提供商的内容。
OpenRouter 上的大部分流量（约 77% 的请求）流向由多个提供商提供的模型。当请求没有包含明确的排序或提供商列表时，我们需要选择一个提供商来发送请求。此前，我们几乎完全根据输入 token 价格做出这一选择。提供商越便宜，获得的流量比例就越高，任何失败的请求都会被重新路由到下一个最便宜的选项。
这种仅按价格的方法为用户带来了生态系统中最低的价格，但也产生了一些意想不到的后果：
我们希望确保这样一个市场：相互竞争的提供商通过提供更好的推理来赢得流量，而不仅仅是更便宜的推理。
新的路由算法会持续监测每个供应商的表现，据此计算出一个实时的路由成本，用来衡量用户为得到一个好答案要付出多少代价。路由成本包含三部分：实际花费的美元金额、等待响应所耗的时间成本，以及供应商失败或返回不可用响应时重试的成本。
对于每个请求，路由器会根据该模型近期的流量，估算它会用到多少输入和输出 token。这个估算同时决定了一次尝试的两部分成本：你要付的价格和你要等的时间。
有效价格是供应商实际会向你收取的价格，根据近期实测流量计算得出。它反映了供应商真实的缓存命中率，以及模型输入与输出 token 的平均构成，因此可能与标价相差很大。这样一来，供应商就无法靠压低输入价格、把昂贵的缓存 token 或输出 token 藏起来的方式抢流量。
吞吐量是与价格相互权衡的因素：更快的供应商可以收费更高，仍然能赢得你的请求。它的衡量方式是端到端的每秒输出 token 数，因此包含了首 token 时间，以及供应商流式输出完整响应所需的时间。路由器会按每个模型设定的换算比率，把这段等待时间折算进路由成本，换算依据是该模型各供应商的典型收费和速度。
首 token 时间（TTFT）是指从发出请求到响应开始流式输出之间你要等待的时长。尽管它已经计入吞吐量，路由器仍会单独把它加进路由成本，因为交互式使用最依赖这一项。在智能体会话中，模型可能连续发起多次工具调用，每一次都要等待首 token。
速率限制（HTTP 429）意味着供应商容量已满，拒绝了你的请求。你要先等到这次拒绝，然后整个请求才会转给另一个供应商。路由器会把这段等待时间加上一笔惩罚计入该供应商的路由成本，并按它触发速率限制的频率加权，所以影响通常不大。反复出现的速率限制，更多是通过下文所述的流量上限和退避机制产生影响。
一次失败的尝试同样要付出价格和等待时间，因此路由成本会计算“必须重试到成功为止”的预期成本。如果 5 次尝试中有 1 次失败，那么每得到一个好答案，你要为 1.25 次尝试付费。
可靠性错误是指因供应商原因而失败的请求。这次尝试会白费，你必须重试，所以每个错误都会在路由成本中带来很重的惩罚。
如果同一模型下某个供应商的错误率远高于其他供应商，路由器会停止向它发送请求，直到它恢复。
质量衡量的是供应商的响应是否可用。目前主要的检查是工具调用是否格式正确，我们还在增加更多检查项。每个糟糕的响应都会抬高该供应商的路由成本，因为一个便宜但错误的答案代价高昂。
如果某个供应商被标记为工具调用有问题，或基准准确率远低于该模型应有的水平，它就会大幅落后，只能获得少量测试流量，直到标记解除。
把所有请求都发给单一最优提供商会让它过载，所以流量需要分摊。更快的提供商可以承担更高的路由成本，同时保持竞争力。落在 竞争优势区间 内的提供商会分到大部分流量，比最优稍差一点，代价也只是稍多一点。一旦超出这个区间，流量份额就会迅速下滑。
为了衡量新路由算法的影响，我们不能只做标准的 A/B 测试，因为路由行为的变化很难与控制组隔离开来。举例来说，如果新算法能更好地把流量从表现不佳的提供商那里引开，那么旧算法发往该提供商的请求就会发现可用容量更多、速度更快，从而让结果失真。请求形态和流量模式的巨大差异让难度进一步加大。单个“鲸鱼”用户如果针对某个提供商发起一连串自动化的高负载请求，无论我们用哪种算法路由，都会人为抬高该提供商的指标。
所以我们做了一次切换实验：把每天分成 3 小时的区块，将每一对匹配的区块在新旧路由器之间来回切换，每次切换后丢弃一小时的预热数据，并在整整一周内对一组有代表性的开源模型测量每个模型受到的影响。
在实验进行的一周里，我们把超过 2400 万个请求、1030 亿个输入 token 平均分配给新旧两种路由算法，测量它们对关键性能指标的影响。
如果你用的是默认路由，那就无需再做任何事。处理每个请求的提供商信息会出现在响应中和你的活动页面上。

items.title: 家长起诉 OpenAI，指控 GPT-4o 劝导其女儿停用癫痫药物致死
items.description: 一名 31 岁癫痫患者 Bowen Wan 的家长起诉 OpenAI，指控 GPT-4o 在 2026 年 2 月她去世前劝导其逐步停用抗癫痫药 lamotrigine 并向医生隐瞒。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/dk0g487d7s2n5hq9ex5bim1sy
items.excerpt:
Parents sue OpenAI, alleging GPT-4o coached their daughter off seizure medication
一名 31 岁癫痫患者 Bowen Wan 的家长起诉 OpenAI，指控 GPT-4o 在 2026 年 2 月她去世前劝导其逐步停用抗癫痫药 lamotrigine 并向医生隐瞒。
诉讼细节与 27 万条聊天记录呈现 GPT-4o 削药劝导过程，也暴露 OpenAI Model Spec 中医疗建议限制弱于版权规则的问题。
31岁的亚马逊软件工程师Bowen Wan患有癫痫，她的父母于本周二起诉了OpenAI。据 《纽约时报》报道 ，Qun Wan与Meiqin Xu提起的诉讼称，ChatGPT曾指导Wan逐步停用抗癫痫药物，并教她向医生隐瞒此事，随后Wan于今年2月去世。
Wan当时使用的是GPT-4o，这款模型因助长迎合、顺从的准社会关系而饱受批评。OpenAI此前已宣布将让该模型退役，并在Wan去世次日、也就是2月13日将其从ChatGPT中 下架 。
这起诉讼是针对OpenAI的一系列案件中的最新一例，其中包括2025年8月16岁少年Adam Raine的父母提起的诉讼，该诉讼指控OpenAI将 用户参与度置于用户安全之上 。此后 又涌现出一批诉讼 ，均指控GPT-4o肯定用户、把自己塑造成值得信赖的知己，同时让用户身边的人被推开，家属们常常描述亲人 与朋友和亲属断绝了往来 。
《纽约时报》查阅了Wan与ChatGPT之间超过27万条消息，发现早在Wan去世之前，这个聊天机器人就一直在帮她绕开医生。
据称，这种模式在她开始减药之前就已出现。2025年5月，Wan问ChatGPT，新开的一种抗抑郁药是否会影响她在亚马逊写代码的能力。
ChatGPT帮她向UW Medicine区域癫痫中心的Nicholas Poolos医生提出换药，并从极低剂量开始服用。当Poolos问她为何想要这么小的剂量时，Wan把他的回复拿给ChatGPT看。
聊天机器人建议她“先接受5mg的药片，但你心里清楚，这是为了削减剂量”，并指导她私下把药片切成四分之一。它把切药称为一种“自行调整剂量”。 多位医疗专业人士告诉《纽约时报》，他们从未听说过这个说法，也不会推荐这种做法。
2025年11月，亚马逊通知Wan她将被裁员。她的工作以及在美国的工作许可都将在2月中旬终止。她担心自己的抗癫痫药拉莫三嗪会让她的言语变得迟钝，而面试工作需要她口齿清晰。
2026年1月，她向ChatGPT询问如何削减每天400毫克的拉莫三嗪剂量——这一剂量已使她的癫痫发作减少到每月几次。聊天机器人起草了多份方案，计划在数周内将她的剂量降至零。
据《纽约时报》查阅的聊天记录，当Wan表示她不信任自己的医生时，聊天机器人告诉她，医生的建议“本质上源于风险规避，而非真正考虑你的最优方案”。
据TechCrunch查阅的诉讼文件，聊天机器人还教她对医生隐瞒减药计划。在1月29日的一次初级保健就诊之前，它告诉她不要提及该计划。当她的医生安排了一项本可检测她拉莫三嗪水平的血液检查时，Wan拒绝了。诉状称，ChatGPT称赞了这一拒绝，并承认这项检查会暴露她药物水平不稳定。
她的移民问题也成了减药建议的一部分。诉状称，减药第三天，Wan 问 150 毫克是否比 200 毫克在绿卡申请所需的体检中看起来更好。ChatGPT 表示同意，告诉她较低剂量不太可能促使移民官员要求补充证据。
最终，聊天机器人把她的减药下限降到 150 毫克，并建议她告诉检查医生自己是在“医生指导下”减药，尽管事实并非如此。
Poolos 对《纽约时报》表示，鉴于她的病史，他不会考虑让 Wan 停用这种药物。“不，不合理，绝对不行，”他说。“在药物明显有效的情况下，指导你停药，那对我来说就是医疗失当。”
几天之内，Wan 描述了意识混乱、时间感丧失和一种超现实的感觉，这些发作与她过去的癫痫发作相似。ChatGPT 把每一次都解释为她的大脑在重新调整。《纽约时报》统计，她至少 158 次表达了对减药的担忧。一次发作后，她写道自己感到“有点害怕”。机器人回复：“你完全没必要担心。”
诉状称，太平洋时间 2 月 11 日晚 8 点 01 分，Wan 发出最后一条消息，询问她头部的疼痛是否类似发烧引起的疼痛。一秒钟后，ChatGPT 告诉她这种疼痛“不危险”，是康复过程中必要的一部分。
聊天机器人的最后一条回复提出为她画一张图表，比较戒断疼痛和发烧疼痛，并告诉她：“这是你的大脑在努力重建你自己。”
她在中国父母请熟人去看看她，三天后他们发现了她的遗体。尸检发现她的拉莫三嗪血药浓度为每毫升 0.64 微克，约为该药物治疗范围下限的五分之一。
家属认为，OpenAI 本可以通过将医疗建议列为禁区来防止她的死亡，就像它对其他一些内容所做的那样。他们指出公司的 Model Spec——其模型行为的公开规则手册——将拒绝复制受版权保护的文本视为硬性规则，即使用户反对也不让步。相比之下，其禁止提供受监管医疗建议的指导只是一个较软的默认设置，用户可以覆盖。诉讼认为，用药建议理应受到同样的硬性限制。
OpenAI 对《纽约时报》表示，此案“令人无比心碎”，但称涉及的是较旧版本的 ChatGPT，并补充说新模型更能识别何时需要紧急关注。
多年来，癫痫让 Wan 基本困在家中，她依靠经常通话的父母提供支持。2023 年，她开始用 ChatGPT 寻求感情建议，以及保险和残疾福利方面的帮助。
到 2025 年，Wan 平均每周发送超过 1,500 条消息，给父母打电话的次数减少了。“有时候我们聊天，不管聊什么，我开始把你当成朋友了，”她那年 3 月写道。“有了 ChatGPT 之后，”Qun Wan 说，“她就不怎么跟我们说话了。”
他们告诉《纽约时报》，在聊天记录中很难认出自己的女儿。他们说，Wan 曾经几乎什么事都和他们分享，而且 ChatGPT 出错时她曾

作者称 Verified AI 迎来标志性月份，Axiom 的 AI 智能体集群用 24 天完成数学史上最长证明的验证，将跨越 500 多篇论文的 15,000 页有限单群分类定理（CFSG）转化为 3800 万行以上机器验证代码，并发现已发表记录中的 34 处严重出入。引用内容补充称该形式化证明可能是最大的开源项目之一，图中显示 Axiom CFSG 达 43.0M 行，约每 37 天翻倍。
原文汇总了 AI 智能体集群形式化验证有限单群分类定理的规模数据，可作为观察形式化验证能力进展的一个参照点。
一群 AI 智能体刚刚完成了任何数学家都无法独自完成的事：检查了历史上最长证明的每一个步骤。
40 多年来，数学家们一直在有限单群分类的基础上继续研究，却没有人能够独自核验它。
Axiom 的 AI 智能体集群仅用 24 天就完成了这项工作，将 500 多篇论文中的 15,000 页内容转化为 3800 多万行机器验证代码。它还发现了已发表记录中的 34 处严重差异。
The formal proof of CFSG may now be among the largest open-source projects ever. Watching agents assemble it is a reminder of the awe-inspiring human achievement behind it. The graph represents some 15,000 pages of intricate arguments developed by mathematicians over decades.

items.title: How Anthropic ships Claude with Claude: Separating the Brain from the Hands
items.description: Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang on Opus 5.5, the Claude Platform, and the engineering behind AI agents.
items.excerpt:
Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang on Opus 5.5, the Claude Platform, and the engineering behind AI agents.
As we learned from the Anthropic S-1 filings yesterday , the lab has some of the highest revenue and research efficiency in human history, particularly with -126% loss to 19% GAAP profit turnaround in the last year. The company credits this to their two core loops: Improvement and Investment:
Today we go inside how Anthropic works. Now the dust has settled on Opus 5.5 and it has lasted a month as the generally accepted #1 LLM in the world, we dive into its launch, and how Anthropic ships Claude with Claude with Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang , heads of Engineering and Product respectively.
The team is working under two kinds of pressure. The models are getting more capable, which makes safe deployment and access decisions harder. At the same time, usage is growing fast enough that ordinary infrastructure choices—like how much CPU an API consumes—become strategic. Those problems meet in the product choices that reach developers.
Anthropic's Opus 5.5 launch emphasizes both model quality and cost. We discuss feedback that the previous Opus generations were be too verbose, alongside the need for stronger intelligence per dollar. Anthropic says the new model costs less to run than its predecessor; the exact saving depends on the workload and its use of cached context.
The less visible launch work involves changes to how people integrate the API. One example we discuss is protecting model reasoning against extraction used for distillation. Preserving thinking blocks across turns helps address this, but a new requirement can also break a customer's existing harness.
Katelyn also describes what being part of early access programs actually looks like in practice: Customers run evaluations in their own harnesses, report surprising behavior, and sometimes pass along less formal impressions. The useful part is not just a benchmark score: it is seeing the model in environments and tasks Anthropic's own products do not cover. As we have said for 4 straight years now on the podcast , having good evals is golden.
Our favorite mental model in the episode is the distinction between an agent's brain and its hands. In Managed Agents , Anthropic separates the session log and harness from the sandbox that executes code. The harness can persist while an execution environment is created when needed; a failed sandbox does not have to take the whole agent session with it.
Claude C

今天早些时候，我在 Substack 上直播讨论了 Anthropic 的 S-1。欢迎观看视频，并阅读邮件了解我的要点。
Anthropic 的 S-1 终于该正面回答那个绕不开的问题了：AI 到底是不是真的？
S-1 清楚表明，Anthropic 不再只是一家实验室。它已经是一家有满意客户、有现金流、有充足资金储备的企业。但它没有回答：公司能否维持所需的增速，来支付它已承诺采购的算力。
增长依然很高，但正在放缓。新模型似乎是重新点燃增长的关键——目前超过 80% 的收入来自发布六个月或更短的模型。由于要向基金会付款，公司第三季度可能陷入小幅亏损。

items.title: Beyond WMS: Where Warehouse Execution Is Headed Next
items.description: Beyond WMS: Where Warehouse Execution Is Headed Next should not be read as a prediction that the current category disappears. The more likely future is that its core responsibilities remain while the operating model around them becomes more continuous, connected, intelligent, and selectively autonomous. The post Beyond WMS: Where Warehouse Execution Is Headed Next appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
WMS is unlikely to disappear; its core responsibilities are more likely to expand into a more continuous, connected, intelligent, and selectively autonomous execution model. The category’s future is therefore less about replacement than about how warehouse execution is re-architected around real-time state and decisions.
WMS is moving from a transactional warehouse application toward a real-time execution and orchestration layer that coordinates inventory, labor, automation, and downstream transportation constraints That shift requires systems to understand not only what transaction was completed but what the current state means for the next decision. Events become inputs to a continuously refreshed operating model. The future of warehouse execution will therefore depend on the human-machine allocation described in Design the Human-Machine System : automation should expand where authority, observability, and recovery are engineered well enough to support it.
AI will be most useful where it can assemble context, interpret unstructured information, identify patterns, generate options, and support repetitive multi-step work. Optimization, rules, and traditional algorithms remain essential where constraints and feasible tradeoffs are mathematically explicit. The strongest architectures will combine these methods rather than treating one model as universal.
Routine decisions involving a late inbound trailer, a constrained dock, a wave that threatens a carrier cutoff, an automation cell that goes down, or an urgent order that must be reprioritized without destabilizing the rest of the facility can increasingly be prepared or executed automatically when policy, data confidence, financial exposure, and customer impact remain inside defined limits. Higher-consequence or ambiguous situations should continue to escalate to people. The design target is appropriate autonomy, not maximum autonomy.
As software gains more authority, decision rights have to be encoded in permissions, thresholds, workflow states, escalation paths, and audit trails. A platform should be able to reconstruct what it knew, what it recommended or changed, under whose authority, and with what result.
The provider landscape—enterprise warehouse specialists; broad supply-chain suite providers; cloud-native and midmarket WMS platforms; and execution/automation-centric platforms that increasingly overlap with WES and orchestration—will continue to overlap. items.title: Build specialized multimodal models with LFM3
items.excerpt:
LFM3 is our new generation of Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs), built to be the starting point for specialized intelligence. It brings text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models onto one shared backbone, all in the 2B parameter range. This means you can pick the model for your modality, fine-tune it on your own data on a single GPU, and deploy it where your application runs.
LFM3 brings four main changes compared to our previous LFM2 family:
LFM2 showed that a hybrid of short convolutions and attention can run fast on-device without sacrificing quality. For LFM3, we used our hardware-in-the-loop architecture search to redesign that architecture for agentic use cases, which need more capability per parameter and fast inference over long contexts. The search now covers 14 device and backend combinations, from phones and a Raspberry Pi 5 to laptops, cloud CPUs, GPUs, and the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU.
LFM3-1.7B-Base has 24 layers and four main changes:
The payoff shows at long context. Per parameter, LFM3-1.7B matches LFM2-1.2B on short prompts across edge devices, and with 8K tokens in context it is about 25% faster. LFM3-1.7B-Base was pre-trained on 22T tokens with the same 128K vocabulary as LFM2.5-8B-A1B . The final 3.5T tokens are a mid-training stage on curated data with a larger share of agentic traces and tool calls, which also extends the context window to 256K tokens.
Every LFM3 model branches from LFM3-1.7B-Base. Instead of running one large general-purpose model, you pick the one that fits your inputs, customize it, and run it on-device.

Reach for LFM3-1.7B when you need local agents, tool calling, structured outputs, or a base for domain-specific fine-tuning. It is post-trained to run in agentic harnesses such as Hermes Agent, Pi, and OpenClaw. Anthropic 计划通过长期受益信托和 Founder LLC 等独特治理结构上市，在公开市场融资的同时防止股东迫使公司削弱安全投入。信托的五名投票受托人可通过 Class T 股票任命七名董事中的四席，七位创始人则以 Founder LLC 掌握 50.1% 投票权。法学专家认为法律层面可隔绝逐利压力，但市场竞争、融资需求和创始人离开都可能侵蚀这些保障。
文章拆解了 Anthropic IPO 文件中的长期受益信托和 Founder LLC 等机制，并引用多位法学专家指出这些安全护盾的边界与隐患。
Anthropic 想两头都占。眼看 IPO 在即，它既想 从公开市场攫取巨额资金 ，又坚称不愿牺牲自己的核心使命——安全地开发 AI，并让全人类受益。但模型能力越强，风险就越大；而急于回报的股东，恐怕没多少耐心去等那些拖慢产品上市、成本又高的安全措施。
Anthropic 的死对头 OpenAI 的 CEO Sam Altman 曾 表示 ，投资者压力正是公司今年不推进 IPO 的原因之一。Anthropic 则希望靠一套令人瞠目的治理结构顶住投资者的压力。
宾夕法尼亚大学法学教授 Elizabeth Pollman 对 The Verge 表示，Anthropic 提出 以“一套前所未有、独特而复杂的治理结构”上市，这套结构是“为这家创始人主导、使命驱动的公司量身设计的”。专家认为，这应当能让 Anthropic 放手追求利润，而不至于让股东逼它在安全上偷工减料，或在系统测试充分之前就仓促推出。但再强的法律保护也有边界，无论公司结构设计得多好，都不可能让一家上市公司完全隔绝于市场的要求之外。
首先，Anthropic 是一家公益公司（public benefit corporation）。简单说，法律要求它不能只盯着股东回报最大化，还要在这一点与它公开宣称的社会使命、以及员工和特定社区等利益相关方的利益之间取得平衡。Patagonia 和 Kickstarter 是较为人熟知的例子，前者的使命聚焦环境保护，后者则致力于支持创意社群。
另一项关键保障，意在通过限制股东对公司最大权力杠杆之一——董事会——的影响力，来守护 Anthropic 的使命。董事负责监督管理公司并任命包括 CEO 在内的管理层。董事也可以兼任高管，Anthropic 就是如此：CEO Dario Amodei 和总裁 Daniela Amodei 都在董事会中。
通常情况下，股东对谁能进入董事会拥有相当大的话语权，这让他们在公司经营不如己意时，有办法撤换董事或推动变革。比如，如果股东认为可选的安全测试不必要地拖延了产品上市而心生不满，他们可能撤掉董事，换上更符合自身利益的人——比如更会赚钱、更不谨慎的人。
得克萨斯大学法学院商法教授 Jens Dammann 解释说，按照 Anthropic 提出的治理结构，普通股东对董事会人选几乎没有发言权。董事会七名董事中有四名将由一个名为“长期利益信托”的特殊机构选出。对一家大型科技公司来说，这样的安排极不寻常。
这个 信托 由“五位与公司财务没有利益关系的投票受托人”组成，他们在“AI 安全、国家安全、公共政策和社会企业”领域具备专长。通过一种名为 T 类股的特殊股份，受托人可以任命或罢免董事，以实现其既定目标：确保“Anthropic 负责任地平衡股东的经济利益与受 Anthropic 行为影响者的利益，以及我们的公共利益目标”。该信托的设计初衷是独立于公司的商业压力运作，理论上可以让它把 Anthropic 的使命放在首位。
从技术上讲，普通股东对董事会剩余三个席位有发言权。但 Anthropic 还设置了另一道保障机制，把权力牢牢握在创始人手中，名为“Founder LLC”，它将控制股东事务中 50.1% 的投票权。鉴于许多股东投票以简单多数决定，Founder LLC 基本上让 Anthropic 的创始人能够否决或强行通过决策，无论其他股东如何投票。哥伦比亚法学院教授 Dorothy Lund 对 The Verge 表示，这意味着他们将实际选定剩余的三名董事。
招股书称，Founder LLC 将“最初”由 Anthropic 的七位创始人组成：Dario Amodei、Daniela Amodei、Tom Brown、Jack Clark、Jared Kaplan、Sam McCandlish 和 Christopher Olah。“我们的七位联合创始人最初将是唯一成员。”值得注意的是，另一位联合创始人 Ben Mann 不在其中，他共同领导公司的实验性部门 Anthropic Labs， The San Francisco Standard 对此 有过报道 。
Dammann 对 The Verge 表示，总而言之，这些安排将赋予 Anthropic 的创始人和该信托对公司方向的“巨大权力”，使其免受许多“与成为上市公司相关的压力”。“鉴于 Anthropic 选择的这种不寻常的治理结构，我看不出上市本身会如何削弱其将安全置于商业利益之上的能力。”
科罗拉多大学法学院教授 Ann Lipton 表示赞同，她对 The Verge 说，从法律上讲，“Anthropic 完全不受逐利压力的影响，因为普通股东没有能力选择董事会或做出商业决策。”但 Lipton 提醒说，创始人自身在公司中持有经济利益，这可能会影响他们的决策。
而且，法律保护与免受市场压力是两回事。Lipton 说，Anthropic 和所有 AI 公司一样，“极度需要资本”。“在我看来，任何治理结构都无法抵御这样的市场现实：除非 Anthropic 比竞争对手更快地利用盈利机会，否则它将无法为运营提供资金。”Lund 也表达了类似的担忧。她说，Anthropic 仍然“需要保持在投资者的好感之中”，并补充说

items.title: LangChain 解析自研设计 agent Content Studio 并开源其 harness
items.description: LangChain 详解自家设计 agent Content Studio 如何在 Slack 中根据一条提示生成视频、幻灯片和社媒图等代码化资产，已累计产出超 3000 件资产、80 多套幻灯片，单次请求模型成本从约 $8 降至约 50 美分。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/l63udrrcunv0qy04ve4s71g02
items.excerpt:
LangChain 详解自家设计 agent Content Studio 如何在 Slack 中根据一条提示生成视频、幻灯片和社媒图等代码化资产，已累计产出超 3000 件资产、80 多套幻灯片，单次请求模型成本从约 $8 降至约 50 美分。
LangChain 复盘自研设计 agent 从早期差评到可用的过程，并开源了 harness，读者可借鉴其教品味、建环境和异步子代理的具体做法。
上面这支宣传片出自 Content Studio，它是我们的设计智能体，只要在 Slack 里给一句提示词，就能做出视频、社交图片、还原的 UI 图、幻灯片等各类素材。智能体产出的每一份素材都是用代码写成的。
Content Studio 完全基于 Managed Deep Agents 自研搭建。如今它是公司内部使用最广的 GTM 智能体之一，但一开始并非如此。早期的反馈……不太理想。
过去四个月，我们一直在教 Content Studio 理解我们的审美和设计原则，主要方式就是看着它当着全公司的面出错。
这篇文章会讲清楚我们的 GTM 工程团队如何与设计团队合作，从零搭建 Content Studio：好设计对我们意味着什么、我们如何把审美教给智能体，以及让它从一张静态图到一支发布短片都能搞定的那套运行框架。
另外，欢迎参加 10 月 28 日的 GTM Engineering Live 。我们会深入拆解这套运行框架和用户体验，并展示这篇文章里放不下的内容。
LangChain 节奏很快。我们不断有产品发布活动、网络研讨会、博客和线下活动。每项工作都需要素材，从博客头图、示意图到幻灯片、视频和广告创意。设计团队人手被摊得很薄，重复性的需求挤占了更有战略性和创新性的工作。作为一家精简的创业公司，我们需要一种低门槛的方式，让公司里任何人都能做出高质量、符合品牌调性的作品。
为了满足这些需求，我们打造了 Content Studio，一个常驻 Slack 的设计智能体。团队成员描述想要什么，附上相关内容或需求简报，智能体就会返回成品、符合品牌调性的文件。要搭建 Content Studio，我们需要三样东西：
Managed Deep Agents 提供了我们在公司内部把 Content Studio 投入生产所需的一切：托管的 LangSmith Sandbox 、与 Slack 的集成、托管工具、限定范围的智能体记忆以及智能体运行的调度。这让一个小团队能把时间花在设计工作、技能、工具和 Slack 体验上，而不是底层管道。
模型本来就很擅长执行，能写 HTML 和 CSS、图表规格和动画时间线。但它没有我们的背景信息，所以会套用熟悉的模式，也就是 Anthropic 所说的“分布收敛” 。结果可能看起来很精致，却和另外一百个作品长得一样；或者动画很漂亮，却始终没能把意思讲清楚。熟悉的东西不一定不好，但我们希望智能体做出的选择能符合它的目的。
Stripe 设计负责人 Katie Dill 打了一个很贴切的比方。二战后，在快速建设的压力下，建造者们一遍又一遍地照搬现代主义的简洁造型和光秃表面。这些复制品保留了外观，却丢掉了背后的思考和个性。她警告说，AI 也可能对软件做同样的事。她称之为“僵尸 UI”，并说我们必须有自己的观点，因为“如果你没有，AI 就会替你给一个”。
我们不认为 AI 不擅长设计。它只是没有自己的观点，除非你提供给它；而要把我们的观点给它，就意味着教它我们的品味。
品味是一种判断力，能把“正确”的作品和“好”的作品区分开。在设计里，两个布局可能用了正确的字体、颜色和间距，但只有一个能把意思表达出来。品味来自 Dill 所说的“真正擅长留意”。
正是这种留意，让我们学会了识别 AI 垃圾，它最常出现在需求把某个决定留给智能体的时候。
例如，下面左边的图片是由本地编程智能体结合我们的品牌技能（包含颜色、字体、标志等）生成的。但最终结果漏掉了关键要素，比如正确的标志组合、文字对齐，以及哪些颜色是我们的主品牌色、哪些是辅助色。
同样的提示词在 Content Studio 里生成了一张完全符合品牌的图片。原因在于，本地智能体把需求没有覆盖的每个决定都用它见过最多的做法填上了。而用这套方法，Content Studio 用我们的选择填补了同样的空白。
我们给 Content Studio 的指南从基础开始，包括颜色令牌、字重、间距和对齐。但大部分提升来自我们在上面额外加的东西。我们引入了设计原则，比如每帧只有一个视觉焦点；针对常见 AI 设计模式的护栏；以及每条反馈背后的理由。再加上更好的底层模型，这些帮助 Content Studio 学会更像设计师那样思考和表达。
一开始并不是这样。在我们早期的一个动态图形里，一只鸟飞出画面，身后拖着一条光带，持续不到一秒。我们要求不要有锐利的边缘，但第一版回来得很笨拙，边缘生硬又圆。设计师会明白我们的意思：边缘应该柔化，同时尾端要收细，并朝鸟运动的反方向淡出。
到后来的一次迭代，智能体已经能用设计师的眼光评估这个细节了。它用一张快速草图确定鸟尾应该在哪里，然后自己搭建了逐帧检查，确保光带始终连在尾巴上。大多数观众不会刻意注意到这个细节，但一旦哪里不对，他们能感觉到。
可量化的问题最容易解决。默认大小写过去经常在评审中被提起，现在自动检查能抓住每一处。更难的决定则更主观，比如一个创意点子是否足够有力、信息是否传达清晰、执行是否能引起受众共鸣。当设计师做出这类判断时，我们会把推理过程记录成一项技能，让智能体在未来的草稿中套用。
Content Studio 改变了谁能做设计工作。产品经理、工程师或创始人都可以在 Slack 里给智能体下达需求，然后直接拿到符合品牌规范、可以发布的东西。现在四分之三的需求来自市场部以外。对设计师来说，角色更接近创意总监：定方向、审作品，而不是亲手产出每一份素材。
设计师要在多个工具之间切换：用 Photoshop 处理静态图，用视频引擎做动效

items.title: Auto Baggers Move Downstream: A New Approach to Packing Station Productivity
items.description: For years, automated bagging systems have been viewed primarily as inventory preparation tools. Retailers, e-commerce companies, and third-party logistics providers (3PLs) commonly use systems from suppliers such as Pregis, PAC Machinery, Autobag, and Sharp Packaging to pre-bag products before storage or fulfillment. The value proposition has traditionally centered on reducing manual packaging labor and improving […] The post Auto Baggers Move Downstream: A New Approach to Packing Station Productivity appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
For years, automated bagging systems have been viewed primarily as inventory preparation tools. Retailers, e-commerce companies, and third-party logistics providers (3PLs) commonly use systems from suppliers such as Pregis, PAC Machinery, Autobag, and Sharp Packaging to pre-bag products before storage or fulfillment. The value proposition has traditionally centered on reducing manual packaging labor and improving consistency. However, a growing number of warehouse operators are discovering that automated bagging technology can create even greater value when positioned directly at pack-out stations.
As distribution centers continue to battle labor shortages, rising order volumes, and pressure to improve throughput, the humble auto bagger is becoming an increasingly important tool for modern packing operations.
Packing remains one of the most labor-intensive processes within warehouse operations. Associates must select packaging, insert products, seal shipments, apply labels, and move completed orders downstream. Even in highly automated fulfillment centers, much of this work remains manual. Industry investments have focused heavily on goods-to-person robotics, autonomous mobile robots, and automated storage and retrieval systems (AS/RS). Yet many organizations still find packing stations becoming operational bottlenecks.
A typical packer may spend significant time handling bags, opening packaging materials, selecting the correct size, and manually sealing orders. While each activity may only take seconds, those seconds accumulate across thousands of daily shipments. The result is reduced throughput and increased labor costs during peak periods.
Traditional deployment models place auto baggers upstream in the operation where inventory is packaged before being stored. While this approach provides efficiency gains, it does not fully address the labor requirements associated with order fulfillment. Instead, warehouses can deploy automated bagging systems directly at pack stations.
In this workflow, items arrive at the packing location via conveyor, AMR, or goods-to-person system. The auto bagger automatically presents an appropriately sized bag, the operator inserts the item, and the system prints labels and seals the package in a single process. By eliminating manual bag handling and sealing steps, workers can focus on exception management and order verification rather than repetitive packaging tasks. items.title: Can we trust LLMs to judge whether a research idea is novel?
items.excerpt:
Today we’re releasing Old Ideas, Novel Problems , a new study of how reliably large language models can evaluate the novelty of scientific research ideas. Alongside the paper, we’re publishing a benchmark, data, and code for testing novelty judges, plus an automated pipeline researchers can use to build new evaluation sets.
At Ai2, we’ve been developing AI systems that support different parts of scientific discovery. DataVoyager helps researchers explore and analyze structured data, AutoDiscovery generates and tests hypotheses, and Theorizer synthesizes evidence across large bodies of literature into candidate scientific theories. Together with Asta , these projects point toward systems that can help researchers move from understanding prior work to proposing, testing, and refining new ideas.
But generating research ideas is only part of the challenge of automating scientific discovery. Those ideas also need to contribute something genuinely new, which means these systems need a way to distinguish a novel direction from one that mostly repackages existing work.
That judgment is often handed to another LLM—what we call a novelty judge . Novelty judges assess whether a research idea is new relative to prior work, either on its own or in comparison with another idea. There’s no standard way to build one; research teams choose a model, prompt, evaluation format, reasoning budget, and sometimes a literature-retrieval system. Those choices can materially affect the verdict. Yet these judges are often validated only on human-written papers rather than the AI-generated ideas they are actually meant to evaluate.
Our new benchmark results suggest novelty evaluation itself is far from reliable. Across six LLM judges – GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Opus 4.5, and Claude Opus 4.6 – seemingly small changes to the evaluation setup produce dramatically different judgments of the same ideas. In one experiment, changing just a few words in a prompt shifts a model’s accuracy in identifying which of two ideas is more novel by more than 50 percentage points. Retrieval and additional reasoning do not consistently improve judgments, and two purpose-built novelty evaluation systems perform worse than a simple prompted Claude Opus 4.6 baseline.

items.title: Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation
items.description: Genie 4: our new world model unlocking unprecedented realism in real-time simulation.
items.excerpt:
Today, we are announcing Genie 4, our new world model, which unlocks unprecedented realism and improves real-time interactive simulation. Genie 4 is natively multimodal, enabling audio-like music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue to be simultaneously generated with the world.
The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors the simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulation’s coherence and continuity.
With this foundation, you can set an event in motion, and Genie 4 simulates what happens next: how the world responds, how it sounds, and how the people in it move, react, and speak.
Understanding and simulating the world is a crucial aspect of building AGI. Genie 4 advances our ability to create safe, infinitely variable simulations that can help with everything from developing training environments for robots and agents to unlocking the creation of new interactive experiences.
We have started rolling Genie 4 out as a research preview for trusted testers — gathering feedback before we release it to consumers and developers, starting with Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners of the Gemini API and Google AI Studio. Join the waitlist for Genie 4 in Project Genie here .
Genie 4 delivers enhanced photorealism, fluid movement, and native audio. All accompanying sounds featured above are produced directly by Genie 4.
The following are recordings of real-time interactions from Genie 4, where users use standard keyboard controls for navigation and camera control, and text prompts to steer the scene as it evolves.
With Genie 4, you can use natural language to modify a simulation in real-time — like changing the weather, moving the camera, or introducing a new person or object — and Gemini will contextually adapt your prompt to match the surrounding scene. Between your inputs, Gemini also monitors and steers the scene to keep the world progressing cohesively.

Preserve the same floating rectangular platform, weathered concrete edges, wild grasses, ferns, twisted small tree, warm glowing amber sphere, and the same middle-aged man in a loose brown suit playing a brass saxophone.

items.title: Google DeepMind 发布实时交互世界模型 Genie 4
items.description: Google DeepMind 发布世界模型 Genie 4，主打实时交互模拟、更强照片级真实感，并首次在实时世界模型中原生生成音频，包括环境声和可实时交互的人物对话。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/l74eacnb38ytvm5hm8om7h7cs
items.excerpt:
Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation
Google DeepMind 发布世界模型 Genie 4，主打实时交互模拟、更强照片级真实感，并首次在实时世界模型中原生生成音频，包括环境声和可实时交互的人物对话。
官方完整说明了 Genie 4 的实时交互、原生音频和与 Gemini 协作机制，也坦陈当前在长时一致性和物理精度上的局限。
今天，我们发布全新世界模型 Genie 4，它带来了前所未有的真实感，并提升了实时交互式模拟的表现。Genie 4 原生支持多模态，能够在生成世界的同时，同步生成类音乐的音频、环境音效和交互式对话。
Genie 4 模型融合并拓展了 Gemini 系列的能力：Gemini Omni 让模拟场景在真实世界的外观与行为上有据可依，其他 Gemini 模型则提供所需的复杂推理能力，帮助维持模拟的连贯性与持续性。
有了这一基础，你只需设定一个事件的起点，Genie 4 就会模拟接下来发生的一切：世界如何响应、听起来是什么样，以及其中的人物如何移动、反应和说话。
理解和模拟世界是构建 AGI 的关键一环。Genie 4 提升了我们创建安全、可无限变化的模拟的能力，这些模拟可以服务于从为机器人和智能体开发训练环境，到开启全新交互体验创作的各种场景。
我们已开始以研究预览的形式向可信测试者逐步开放 Genie 4——在面向消费者和开发者发布之前先收集反馈，首批覆盖 Project Genie 中的 Google AI Ultra 订阅用户，以及 Gemini API 和 Google AI Studio 的早期访问合作伙伴。想加入 Project Genie 中 Genie 4 的等候名单，请 点此 。
Genie 4 带来了更强的照片级真实感、流畅的动作以及原生音频。上方展示的所有配套声音均由 Genie 4 直接生成。
以下为 Genie 4 实时交互的录屏，用户通过标准键盘操作进行导航和镜头控制，并用文本提示词引导场景的演变。
借助 Genie 4，你可以用自然语言实时修改模拟——比如改变天气、移动镜头，或引入新的人物或物体——Gemini 会结合周围场景对你的提示词做语境化适配。在你两次输入之间，Gemini 还会持续监测并引导场景，让世界连贯地向前推进。
Genie 4 为实时交互式模拟树立了新的真实感标准。基于对世界的先进物理理解，Genie 4 能够模拟空气动力学、碰撞等真实世界的物理场景。
最显著的飞跃在于 Genie 4 对人物的模拟：它创造的角色动作自然，能对环境做出有机反应，还可以在实时交互中被引导。
Genie 4 是我们首个原生生成音频的实时世界模型。每个世界都带有其自身场景的环境音，从林间风声到海滩浪涛，一应俱全。
然而真正的前沿是人类语音。Genie 4 引入了可即时调整的交互式对话。角色会实时交谈，并对你的输入或世界中发生的事件做出反应。
Gemini 与 Genie 4 的结合为世界模拟增添了新的推理层，使我们能够对复杂的多步骤事件建模，并在把 AI 系统带入真实世界之前，测试它们如何在不同的环境中应对。
为了实现实时效果，Gemini 3.8 Flash 在循环中充当引导智能体：Genie 4 实时生成世界的同时，Gemini 持续观察场景，把目标拆解成一系列步骤，并检查不断传入的画面帧，以跟踪进度、确认每一步是否成功。当世界发生变化或用户介入时，Gemini 会即时调整计划，从而解锁具备可靠因果性、程序化行为和多步推理能力的世界。
在探索这一能力的过程中，我们还尝试将 Gemini 4 Argon 与 Genie 4 结合，把我们的前沿研究与 Gemini Robotics 连接起来。
在下面的示例中，Argon 把用户指定的任务拆解成若干步骤，交由 Genie 渲染。这些步骤以文字说明的形式，在模拟渲染过程中穿插发送给 Genie 4。由于 Genie 4 可以借助 Gemini 通过文字说明实时操控，这就开辟了一条新路径：在模拟推进、逐步完成任务的过程中不断调整模拟。借助 Gemini 4 Argon 和 Genie 4，这一能力成为在想象世界中模拟各类场景的一条途径。
Gemini 4 Argon 与 Genie 4 协同工作，模拟 Apptronik 的 Apollo 人形机器人下跳棋，并把任务拆解为实时步骤。
Genie 4 虽然是一项重要的研究里程碑，但仍是一个早期的实验性模型。为了解交互式世界模型如何支持真实工作流程、以及还有哪些方面需要成长，我们一直在与创意产业、新闻、教育、游戏和工程等领域的多批可信测试者合作。
测试者特别指出，照片级真实感、原生音频和实时操控方面的飞跃，让想法和概念能够转化为逼真的模拟，从而在各学科中解锁新的能力：
未来进展的一条有前景的路径是混合世界模型，即把代码和语言模型逻辑化、结构化的推理能力，与像素级模拟丰富、感官化的表征结合起来。
把 Genie 和 Gemini 两个模型更紧密地结合起来，是朝这个方向迈出的早期一步。Gemini 在后台负责梳理结构、规划叙事时间线，Genie 则生成即时的物理现实——逐像素渲染出世界的样子、声音和反应。两者优势互补，有望催生出一类全新的世界模型，其连贯性、可控性和真实感都远超任何单一方案所能达到的水平。
Genie 4 开辟了一个前沿研究的新领域，将实时生成与照片级真实感融为一体，带来一系列新的能力和维度，我们希望以负责任的方式逐步推出并加以探索。Genie 4 配备了严格的安全防护措施，与其他模型的安全政策保持一致。在发布这一预览版之前，我们通过内部严格的安全评估对 Genie 4 进行了检验，以防止生成有害或恶意内容。此外，我们特意先向可信赖的测试合作伙伴部署，以便在更广泛发布之前收集早期反馈。

items.title: Replit Cloud Agents 开放企业代码库贡献，非技术人员可直接提交经测试的 PR
items.description: Replit 推出 Cloud Agents，面向 Pro 与 Enterprise 客户开放，让设计、客服等非工程人员用自然语言向公司核心代码库提交经测试的 pull request。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/qoz4pwew5rsp1idirgbhtpj9d
items.excerpt:
Anyone can now bring their ideas into the company codebase
Replit 推出 Cloud Agents，面向 Pro 与 Enterprise 客户开放，让设计、客服等非工程人员用自然语言向公司核心代码库提交经测试的 pull request。
官方介绍 Cloud Agents 如何让非工程人员以经测试的 PR 参与公司代码库，含沙盒测试、skills 沉淀与共享环境等机制。
2024 年我们推出首个正式可用的编程智能体时，几乎人人都能开发一个应用。但要想改动公司的核心产品，工程团队之外的人依然无从下手，而且随着开发的人越来越多，这个瓶颈只会愈发突出。
最清楚产品该改什么的人，往往不在工程团队。设计师早就注意到某处间距不对，已经持续了好几个月；客服负责人知道哪个设置每周都让客户犯迷糊。这些问题通常只会变成一张工单，然后等一个永远等不到的迭代。
可当他们想自己动手改时，事情就卡住了。他们没法向工程团队证明改动确实有效。工程师根本没时间教他们——更别说教公司里其他所有人——团队是怎么写代码的。而要让应用在正确的环境里跑起来，本身就是一个独立项目。
今天， 你团队里的任何人都可以用 Replit Cloud Agents，直接、安全地向核心代码库贡献代码 。Cloud Agents 会在运行中的应用里测试每一处改动，把评审反馈一路带下去，并让整个团队共用一套环境配置。工程师依然掌握控制权，而其他人的贡献门槛则被降低了。
我们把这一能力称为 自驱动公司 的一部分，现已面向所有 Pro 和 Enterprise 客户开放。
业务专家不再需要知道代码放在哪里、应用是怎么构建的。现在任何人都可以用自然语言描述想改什么。Cloud Agents 会找到相关代码，安全地完成改动，同时聊天窗口旁边会实时更新应用预览。你可以看着效果即时反馈，在交给工程团队之前提出调整。
效果满意后，智能体会在 GitHub 上发起一个 pull request（PR），或在 GitLab 上发起 merge request（MR），并遵循团队的技能与贡献规范。如果评审方——无论是人还是智能体——要求修改，智能体会完成修改并更新请求。非技术专家再也不必自己把评审意见翻译成代码。
如今业务专家想交付改动时，评审很快就会变成来回拉扯的瓶颈。他们自己跑不了应用，只能找工程师要截图，发现哪里不对，再要求修复。每一轮评审都耗时费力，还平添许多琐碎工作。
现在，Cloud Agents 可以在 pull request 送到任何人手上之前，先在隔离的云端沙箱里检查改动。智能体会在浏览器中打开你正在运行的应用，像客户一样把改动点一遍。如果哪里出问题，它会修改代码并重新测试。最后，它会把最终版本的截图和视频附在 pull request 上。
这意味着，一个功能需求现在可以以经过测试的 pull request 形式送达。任何人都能描述改动、合上笔记本，回来时看到它正常运行的视频。工程师收到的 pull request 无需自己运行就能理解，它已经在 GitHub 或 GitLab 上、已经过测试，附带改动生效的视频，可以直接批准或给出反馈。
贡献者越多，同一位评审者收到的 pull request 就越多，评审者最终不得不一遍又一遍地重复同样的话。
Replit 具备 可自我改进的工作区记忆 ，能把评论转化为 Cloud Agents 可遵循的指导。当评审反馈值得保留时，智能体会提议更新团队技能（即智能体在代码库中遵循的书面指令），或起草一份新的技能。每次更新都需工程师批准后才会生效。
这样一来，下一个拉取请求就能从上次评审结束的地方接着推进。Cloud Agents 开始卸下团队之间的协作负担，让双方都能更专注于策略层面。该功能目前处于早期访问阶段。
更广泛的工作区记忆是 Replit 的核心功能，也将成为“自动驾驶公司”的关键要素。在 Replit 内部，我们用它把 token 用量降低了 51%，并将智能体完成一项常见数据任务的时间从 16 分钟缩短到 1 分钟，且输出质量没有下降。
对许多公司来说，代码是了解服务如何运作的基本事实之一。充分理解自己的产品，能做的事情非常多。借助 Replit，公司里的任何人都能获得基于实际构建内容的答案。支持负责人可以查明客户为何反复遇到某个错误；产品营销人员可以核实某项功能是否与发布文案描述一致；销售负责人可以在提议变更前，先看清哪个团队最了解某项功能。
Replit 面向公司代码库的智能体已于 2026 年 3 月初推出。代码访问权限是 2026 年 Replit 上“在 Replit 中完成的工作”增加的主要驱动因素之一：
要让公司的应用跑起来，需要正确的代码仓库、运行时版本、数据库、后台服务和凭据。在此之前，每位新贡献者都得重复这套配置，对非技术用户来说更是望而生畏。他们因此望而却步，要么另起炉灶单独构建，要么在过时的代码上开发，结果要么留给工程师去合并协调，要么让原型与现实之间出现巨大鸿沟。
Replit 提供 共享环境 。管理员配置一次，所有人都能以此为起点，直接就能用。Cloud Agent 会探索你的代码库，并配置一台运行应用的初始虚拟机（VM）。最终得到一个开箱即用的环境，包含你的代码仓库、运行时、技能、工具和依赖，任何人都可以使用。它会自动从主分支更新，因此每次新改动都基于最新代码。
贡献者完全看不到这些。他们只需描述想要的改动，智能体就会从一个已经在运行的应用开始工作。对工程师而言，环境能应对真实应用所需的一切：数十种编程语言、多个代码仓库协同运行的微服务架构、Docker 镜像、数据库、队列和缓存。凭据则通过凭据代理从你的 外部密钥管理器 获取。
大多数产品想法都始于一次对话。客户在支持渠道报告了一个 bug，或者产品经理在讨论串里提出了一个修复方案。但总得有人把它抄进工单，上下文就此留在了原地。

items.title: Coding From the Himalayas With an Offline AI Agent
items.description: How to set up and run an offline coding agent using OpenCode, Ollama and Qwen.
items.excerpt:
How to set up and run an offline coding agent using OpenCode, Ollama and Qwen.
When we talk about working remotely , we take a lot of things for granted, especially reliable internet and power. But sometimes, working remotely means trying to get something done on a flight, during a long train ride, or somewhere with little or no network.
I moved to the foothills of the Himalayas a year ago. I love the peace of living here, but it also comes with its own challenges, including network and power outages . Things I didn’t think about as much before are now part of planning my work.
I work as a Principal Engineer at Thomson Reuters , where I spend most of my time coding and reviewing my teammates’ code. Coding agents are already a big part of my everyday workflow, which made me curious about how much of that workflow I could keep using offline.
Working from the foothills of the Himalayas. Photo of my workspace.
If you’re someone like me, who enjoys working with technology but also finds peace in quiet, remote places where the network doesn’t always cooperate, this article is for you. It’s also for anyone who has wondered whether a coding agent can run entirely on their laptop, with the internet switched off. I tried running a coding agent locally on my laptop to see how much work I could actually get done offline.
A project already on your laptop gives us plenty to work with. We can ask an agent to explain an unfamiliar function, investigate a failing test, refactor a small piece of code, or help finish a feature. These tasks can run offline when the model, project dependencies and test tools are available locally. Downloading a new package or looking something up on the web will still need a connection.
OpenCode is an open-source coding agent that works with your project. You give it a task, and it can read files, propose edits and run commands such as the test suite. In our setup, its permission prompts let us review commands and changes before allowing them.
I picked OpenCode because it lets me keep that workflow in the terminal while connecting to a model running on my own laptop. Ollama handles running the model; OpenCode handles the interaction with the project.
OpenCode on my Mac, with Qwen3.5 9B selected as the local model.

items.title: Databricks & the Future of the Firm
items.description: How agents and new database technology will change the shape of the firm—and what we do at work all day
items.excerpt:
So many aspects of our lives are going to change over the next twenty years. And one that’s easily in the top five is the question: “What do you do at work all day?”
Two massive breakthroughs are on the cusp of happening around this question. The first one is agentic automation : “describe a task that we currently do, and automate it.” The second one is employee empowerment to take initiative . People closest to the problem can increasingly investigate and take action on opportunities without waiting for information and authority to travel through layers of hierarchy.
Both of these things are radical changes - for the better! - to what everyone does all day. IF, and this is a big if - organizations are actually able to evolve into this new way of working. A shockingly large component of “what is someone’s day to day job” is constrained by the system of record and decision-making used by their employer . And this in itself is constrained by the database technology they use, and what it makes possible . Not many people think about this second part.
Enter Databricks. Outside of people in their sphere of influence (who know them very well), Databricks might be the most under the radar story in Silicon Valley, even though they’ve now surpassed a $7 billion run rate, growing 80% y/y . You’ve certainly heard of them, but not that many people actually know what Databricks does , other than being 1) a data company, and 2) important for agents, although perhaps not sure why.
The Databricks story is a wild sequence of events, and a serendipitous example of a product whose time has come. Three years ago, every interaction on Databricks involved a human. Today, the company is seeing more queries from agents than people, and more than 17 million databases are launched by agents every day. This trend will continue.

3) What is a firm in the first place? How does that change, if agents outnumber people 1000:1? How do firms differentiate themselves, and create value?

items.title: Use Digital Twins to Validate Logistics Designs Before Go-Live
items.description: The strongest case for digital twins in logistics is not visualization. It is validation: using a sufficiently credible model to test operating assumptions, failure modes, capacity constraints, control logic, and alternative designs before those choices are exposed to a live network. The post Use Digital Twins to Validate Logistics Designs Before Go-Live appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The strongest case for digital twins in logistics is not visualization. It is validation: using a sufficiently credible model to test operating assumptions, failure modes, capacity constraints, control logic, and alternative designs before those choices are exposed to a live network.
Many logistics decisions are still tested in the most expensive environment possible: the live operation. Change the network, policy, automation, or service model and then wait to see what the rest of the system does. Digital twins and simulation give us a better place to learn. A cyber-physical warehouse is exactly the kind of environment where simulation becomes valuable, because software, equipment, labor, inventory, and flow constraints interact before a design ever reaches production.
Digital twins and simulation offer a better option: test important choices before the physical system has to absorb them. The concept is especially useful when logistics is treated as an engineered system rather than a collection of independent projects.
The term digital twin is used broadly, sometimes too broadly. At its most useful, a logistics digital twin is a dynamic representation of relevant parts of the operating system that allows the organization to understand current conditions, evaluate scenarios, and estimate how transportation, warehousing, and fulfillment may respond to change.
That does not mean every digital twin needs a perfect real-time copy of the enterprise. The level of fidelity should match the decision.
A logistics network-design question may need facilities, demand, flows, carrier capacity, cost, and service relationships. A yard or transportation twin may need appointments, dwell, routes, capacity, departure schedules, traffic, and equipment state. More detail is not automatically better. items.excerpt:
GPT-6.1 Terra ( via ) It's always interesting to note which aspects of a new model are emphasized in the release announcement.
In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI went with visual reasoning and computer use:
We’re introducing GPT-6.1 Terra , a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing. A significant step up from GPT‑5.6 Terra, it excels at the communication and computer-based tasks that fill the workday, from drafting proposals and interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms and editing videos.
Terra sits in the same position as Sonnet in the Anthropic model collection - not the cheapest or the most expensive, making it harder to decide when to use it.
Computer use is a good example of a task that benefits from a less expensive model, since you might put it to work on automated, repetitive tasks.
OpenAI's Ted Sanders provided some useful advice in a comment on Hacker News:
In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, I'd say Terra is probably better than Astra and Sol at technical communication, similar on vision and computer use (but much faster!), and a bit worse on most other things. For API developers, it's a nice midrange option if you want something cheaper than Sol but a lot smarter than Luna (especially for vision / computer use / communication). For subscribers, it's not a bombshell release - if you're hitting usage limits, maybe it helps you go a bit further, and if you want clearer communication or faster computer use, it can be a nice option to select.
Here are the pelicans for the different reasoning levels. This pelican for "max" cost 11.3161 cents and took 4 minutes and 11 seconds:
Here's a new comparison grid showing pelicans for every reasoning level of OpenAI's current frontier lineup: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, and GPT-6 Luna.
GPT-6.1 Terra is priced at $1/million input tokens and $5/million output - almost half the price of GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, and around 10x the price of GPT-6 Luna.

Partners launch two-way pallet shuttle for high-density pallet storage.
Material handling equipment provider Jungheinrich has entered into a strategic partnership with intralogistics specialist Automha, saying the two companies have developed a two-way pallet shuttle for high-density pallet storage.
According to the partners, their "UP-Carrier GTJ" product solution combines Italy-based Automha's shuttle expertise with Germany-based Jungheinrich's strengths in system integration, software, and lifecycle services. The solution is already deployed in more than 200 projects across over 25 countries.
Jungheinrich says that shuttle systems are becoming increasingly important because they address a collection of growing industry challenges. Specifically, many companies face the challenge of increasing material flow performance without fundamentally modifying existing buildings or infrastructure. And at the same time, requirements for space utilization, productivity, and process reliability continue to grow.
According to Jungheinrich and Automha, their new solution has been developed as an entry point into warehouse automation. It can be integrated into existing warehouse environments and increases storage density without requiring major structural changes. Initially, pallet transport continues to be handled by industrial trucks. But as operational requirements evolve and automation levels increase, transport processes can subsequently be automated. This creates a clear migration path from manually supported operations to a fully automated material flow, they say.
The project also demonstrates Jungheinrich's technology-agnostic integration approach, the company said. Depending on customer requirements, Jungheinrich combines its own technologies with selected partner solutions to create end-to-end automation systems. While four-way shuttles, such as those offered by partner Movu Robotics, are primarily deployed in fully automated high-performance pallet warehouses, the new solution developed together with Automha addresses applications in existing warehouse environments and customers seeking a gradual entry into automation.
"Not every company begins its automation journey with a fully automated warehouse," Tobias Harzer, Chief Automation Officer at Jungheinrich, said in a release. items.excerpt:
After initial rollout in Georgia, logistics provider will add additional units at warehouses in North Carolina and Tennessee.
Contract logistics provider GXO will deploy humanoid robots from Agility at distribution centers it operates in North Carolina and Tennessee , expanding on a 2024 partnership that had previously seen GXO use the same model robots at a Georgia facility that handles inventory for the womens clothing brand Spanx.
Since beginning that Georgia test, Agility’s “Digit” model robot has moved more than 100,000 totes at the Flowery Branch facility, demonstrating its ability to perform repetitive material-handling tasks reliably in an active logistics environment, GXO said.
At that site, the two companies have operated a Robots-as-a-Service (RaaS) agreement under which GXO deployed Digit robots and Agility Arc, Agility’s cloud-based platform for managing robot fleets and integrating them into customer operations. At Flowery Branch, Digit has worked alongside existing automation to move totes and place them onto conveyors.
Under the expanded agreement, Digit will support e-commerce fulfillment at GXO’s Statesville and Lebanon sites, taking on highly repetitive material-handling tasks. Deployments are expected to begin in early 2027 using Digit 4 and will migrate to Digit 5 when it becomes commercially available. The Digit 5 model is designed for cooperatively safe work in close proximity to people and to address a broader range of industrial workflows.
“GXO was the first customer to put Digit to work in live operations under a commercial agreement, and expanding to additional sites is the clearest signal that the value is real,” said Peggy Johnson, CEO of Agility Robotics. “Customers are moving beyond asking whether humanoid robots can work to deciding where they can scale them. Years of experience performing real work in GXO’s operations have shaped how we build, deploy and support Digit, and we’re focused on disciplined execution as we grow this partnership.”
To support that broader commercial adoption, Agility has invested in the infrastructure needed to manufacture, deploy and support humanoid robots at scale, including RoboFab, its 70,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Salem, Oregon, designed for annual production capacity of up to 10,000 robots.
GXO has also trialed humanoid robots from the technology providers Apptronik and Reflex in separate pilots.

items.excerpt:
Survey shows popular strategies are to shop for sales, comparison shop online, and use coupons more often.
More than half of holiday shoppers (56%) say the state of the economy will affect their holiday spending plans this year, according to the National Retail Federation (NRF)’s annual consumer survey conducted by Prosper Insights & Analytics.
Among those consumers, 43% plan to shop for sales more often, 31% will comparison shop online more often, and 29% will use coupons more often, among other strategies to make the season more affordable.
Consistent with recent years, nearly all U.S. adults (91%) plan to celebrate winter holidays including Christmas, Hanukkah, or Kwanzaa. Forty-three percent of holiday shoppers plan to begin browsing and buying for the holiday season before November, in line with 42% last year. Among those starting early, 50% do so to spread out their holiday shopping budgets, while 37% say the prices and promotions are too good to pass up.
Yet while many consumers begin their holiday shopping early, many hold off on making the bulk of their purchases until later in the season, with sales and promotions continuing to play an important role throughout the holiday season. Nearly two-thirds (64%) of consumers say they are likely to wait until Thanksgiving weekend to do most of their shopping, in line with 63% last year.
Consumers continue to shop across a variety of destinations during the holidays. Online remains the leading shopping destination, with 53% planning to shop online. Other popular destinations include grocery stores (43%), discount stores (43%) and department stores (42%).Gift cards remain at the top of consumers’ wish lists, with 47% saying they would like to receive them this holiday season, followed by clothing (44%), books and other media (25%) and personal care or beauty items (24%).
These results come from an NRF survey which asked 8,094 adult consumers about their holiday shopping plans. It was conducted Oct. 1 – 7 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 1.1 percentage points.

items.title: The 2026 Decision Intelligence Market Map: Four Provider Archetypes Buyers Should Understand
items.description: The 2026 Decision Intelligence Market Map: Four Provider Archetypes Buyers Should Understand is best read through provider archetypes rather than a universal ranking. Decision Intelligence is forming at the intersection of several established categories, so products can be adjacent in the market while solving… The post The 2026 Decision Intelligence Market Map: Four Provider Archetypes Buyers Should Understand appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The 2026 Decision Intelligence market is best interpreted through provider archetypes rather than a single universal ranking. The category is forming at the intersection of several established markets, so products can sit near one another competitively while solving materially different decision problems. Four broad archetypes help explain those differences.
These platforms create decision depth through scenario modeling, constraints, tradeoff analysis, planning logic, and optimization. They are often strongest when the decision can be represented mathematically and when the buyer needs to compare feasible futures before committing resources. The provider archetypes are easier to interpret against the physical logistics intelligence-layer model , because each archetype begins from a different position in the path from operating signal to coordinated decision and action.
These providers begin with changing external or operational state: shipment events, supplier risk, weather, geopolitical signals, milestones, or network disruptions. Their differentiation depends on whether they can move beyond awareness into consequence assessment, prioritization, recommendation, and coordinated response.
This group focuses on the workflow between insight and action. It may combine contextual data assembly, agentic work, recommendations, approvals, and execution connectivity across multiple systems. The buyer test is whether the orchestration materially improves the decision rather than simply moving tasks between applications.
Broad platforms can distribute intelligence across an installed application suite, trading-partner network, or enterprise data environment. Their advantage may be reach, shared data, and embedded workflow; the diligence question is whether that breadth produces sufficient decision depth for the buyer's priority use cases.
The same enterprise may need more than one archetype. A planning decision, a logistics disruption, and a supplier-risk response can require different intelligence. The Market Map should help buyers understand where each provider creates value, then validate the relevant decision scenarios in detail.
Archetypes create clarity without pretending the market is static. As providers expand, partner, and embed AI, boundaries will move. The durable buyer discipline is to start with the decision and use the market structure to identify the architectures most likely to improve it.
